Description loop (2026-08-30_204911, claude-fable-5, 23 queries split 14 train / 9 held-out, 3 runs per query with early stop, 3 iterations): the original description scored 13/14 train and 8/9 held-out; both proposed candidates scored 13/14 train and 7/9 held-out, so `best_description` is the original and the frontmatter was left unchanged.

The original's two misses are both should-fire queries phrased as questions about the ritual's rules: 'the check is warning about unfilled stuff in SES-004 but this conversation created SES-006' (1/3) and 'i committed the log entry itself but the append says up to date' (0/3). Every hard negative passed (13/13).

Both candidates added an 'Also use for questions about the ritual's rules' clause. It recovered those two queries and cost two held-out hard negatives: 'How does the session tool decide which SES file is current' (3/3 fired, iteration 2 and 3) and 'the readme is stale, update it' (2/3 and 3/3), plus the train query 'set it up so claude automatically does the session-start reading' (3/3 and 2/3). The boundary between a question about the ritual and a question about the tool is where this description trades recall for precision.

Tier sweep (tiers/, same 23 queries, --no-early-stop, 3 runs each, current description): passes 21/23 fable-5, 22/23 opus-5, 19/23 sonnet-5, 15/23 haiku-4.5. Should-fire queries passed: 9, 9, 6, 2 of 10; mean fire rate on should-fire queries 90%, 83%, 53%, 23%. Hard negatives declined: 12, 13, 13, 13 of 13.

No tier over-triggers: across 4 tiers x 13 hard negatives x 3 runs the only fires are fable-5 on 'set it up so claude automatically does the session-start reading' (2/3) and 'the readme is stale, update it' (1/3). Every miss on haiku and sonnet is a should-fire query that did not fire.

Two should-fire queries fire on every tier (3/3 each): 'ok that commit landed, do the log entry' and 'three commits in a row without logging anything'. Both name the log entry explicitly. The queries that separate the tiers never name the skill's vocabulary: 'stepping away for a couple weeks' (haiku 0/3, others 3/3), 'was the set-favorites swift thing actually verified' (haiku 0/3, sonnet 0/3, opus 2/3, fable 3/3), 'the append put in a skeleton for a commit i didn't make' (fable 3/3, all others 0/3).

The description loop's fable-5 baseline used early stopping (rates over 2 or 3 attempts); the tiers/ fable-5 figure is the full-N re-measurement of the same description and set and agrees on pass count (21/23 both). The two are not the same denominator and are not quoted against each other.

The measurement runs each query in a throwaway project root containing only the aliased skill (--setting-sources project), so no co-installed neighbour (run-scripts, documentation-and-adrs, domain-modeling) competed for the query and the model could not inspect a repository before deciding; recon-then-consult was not available to it.

synthesize-scenarios.ts refused to run against the skill directory or the repo (40 copies of the description leaked into its prompt via evals/results transcripts and via the neighbour sweep quoting the session skill itself); the set was generated from a SKILL.md-only copy with a neighbour project holding every other skill. Its inventory listed 'Gotchas' as a capability and the phrase rule as the only non-goal; the queries do not inherit either.
